utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was told who was seen and what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the fact that Alija Izetbegovic, the president of the SDA party and the president of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time, in June 1991 sent a public appeal to members of the Muslim ethnicity not to respond to the draft calls and not to join the JNA? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the order of the presidency of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which was made on January 9th, 1991, about the disbanding of all armed units that were not part of the armed units of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the police?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't follow these events because at that time it was already clear to me what the JNA was, so I did not follow these events and these orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand me fully. I didn't see these were news. I said this was an order of the presidency.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in August of 1991, on Mount Igman, a meeting was held, an extended meeting of the SDA, with all presidents of municipal councils of SDA, and the topic was the preparation for the war of SDA?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that fact, because at that time I was not a member of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, for the sake of clarity, could you tell us where Mount Igman is, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, could you answer this question or could you confirm that Mount Igman is above the city of Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's where it is even today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you became a member of the SDA in September of 1991, did somebody tell you about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that at that meeting the Crisis Staff was formed and also the security commission of the SDA for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no evidence about that meeting that has been testified to by any witness in this case, number one; number two, this witness did not talk about it and says he didn't know about it. It was prior to him joining the SDA. Therefore, they're putting in evidence through another witness which -- or they're referring to evidence which has never -- they're referring to information which has never been admitted in this case, and therefore it's an improper question, Your Honour. These are facts that aren't in evidence, especially after he's indicated he wasn't there. Now it's question after question. What they're doing is putting in all this other information. If they have a witness who wants to testify about this meeting, fine, let them put that in, but this is basically sneaking evidence in where there is no witness who has testified to any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. I was waiting for the interpretation. The objection is sustained. You can't go on asking a witness about matters which he could not have been aware of because he wasn't a member of the party at that time. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just on that particular topic: If Mr. Pisarevic wants to put his case to witnesses what he says is the true situation, then of course the Prosecution invites him to comply with the Rule. However, if a witness doesn't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- about that particular subject, then he is not obliged to put his case, what he says is the truth about the matter to a witness who says: "I don't know anything about that."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to remind, if I may, the Trial Chamber that the issue of the meeting on Mount Igman did not appear before the Trial Chamber for the first time now. The same question was asked of Mr. Sulejman Tihic and Izet Izetbegovic. But at any rate, if Mr. Fitozovic doesn't know anything about it, I will ask no further questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The point is, with this particular witness, he wasn't a member, so he can't testify to what he couldn't have known.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you became a member of the SDA in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: According to what you told us, you became a member of the municipal board, you immediately became a member of the executive board of the party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You were not a member of the executive board?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to be a member of the executive board of the SDA party, you had to be a member of the municipal board of the SDA; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no municipal board of the SDA, if I may assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: There was the town board of the SDA; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This town board of the SDA, did it exist in the whole territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did this town board of the SDA have any other local communes that would also be covered by it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the reason for this was because in the Samac municipality --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Bosanski Samac. Thank you. That in the local communes there were no villages inhabited by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So there was only the town board of the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And you became a member of the executive board of the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In this capacity you probably attended the session held on the 19th of September, 1991. At that session the political and security situation in the municipality of Samac and in the Doboj region and in Bosnia-Herzegovina was discussed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly you were not at the session, or is it that you don't remember that this session happened and that you -- that this topic was discussed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that such a session was held, and I do not recall this topic being on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in September, the Crisis Staff of the Party of Democratic Action was established for Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in September the commission for security, or the security commission, of which you were a member and indeed the chairman, was formed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, its name was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was the name of the commission Komisija Sigurnost, that being the Croatian term for security, not Bezbjednost, that being the Serbian term?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Sigurnost.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: However, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the term "Bezbjednost was mostly used; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that one and the same thing, Bezbjednost and Sigurnost?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it's one and the same thing, but this commission was called Komisija Sigurnost.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that this commission was indeed established in September 1991 and that you were the chairman of the commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, what was the main task of this commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already explained what its main task was. I did it yesterday or the day before. So my answer would be the same as the one that I had already furnished.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was one of the tasks of the commission to structure the documents, such as the organisational plans, mobilisation plans, things like that, war plans?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Yet according to what you told us, Mr. Fitozovic, in September you became the commander of an armed unit that was established.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No such unit was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then: When did you establish this unit, this armed unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not an armed unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This unit and its members, at least some of the members, were they not armed with automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you not seek weapons for this unit from Mr. Sulejman Tihic and from Mr. Izet Izetbegovic, the president and the vice-president of the Democratic Action Party in Bosanski Samac respectively?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you requested this from them at the session of the executive board of the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, where did you request this from them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will respond, although I do not feel an obligation to do so. On my -- as I walked around the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you answer all questions put to you by counsel. The Trial Chamber is following the questions, the Prosecution is following the questions. If the questions are objectionable on any ground at all, either the Prosecution will say so or the Trial Chamber will say so, and in that case, you don't answer the question; otherwise you answer the questions put to you by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, as I prepared for this cross-examination, I read some documents that were disclosed to me in the course of the proceedings by the Prosecution. In one such document I found the following words: "At the same time, in the party, we set up the Crisis Staff, the command, and we set up the required documents, such as the war plan, et cetera. Alija Fitozovic was in charge of these things, since no other Muslim wanted to join in and become the commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What is he referring to? He said "some documents." I'd like to know what he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, to identify the document from which the information --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If he's talking about a transcript, a statement of someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Counsel. Can you identify the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I failed to do so, Your Honours. These are the memoirs of Mr. Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Then I'd have an objection. Number one, we attempted to introduce the memoirs of Sulejman Tihic. Counsel -- one of the counsel, I think Mr. Pantelic, objected, and all counsel from the Defence fought us for introducing that. So those are not before the Court at this time. So what counsel is trying to do is take statements from Mr. Tihic and use those against this other witness. Mr. Tihic testified. You can use Mr. Tihic's testimony and argue, at the end of the case, Tihic said this, Fitozovic said this. What they are trying to do is impeach Witness Fitozovic with statements made by Tihic. Whenever that is has happened we've objected. And they said you can't impeach one witness with the statement of another. And that's what they're trying to do here. They would not let that document in which it would have been in evidence, but it wasn't, which it's fine, but now they're trying to back door everything in and they're trying to use it as a piece of evidence, which it isn't right now. And number two, they're trying to impeach one witness with the statement of another witness and you just can't do that. I know they won't allow that in the United States, or Great Britain or I don't think any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The procedures don't allow that here either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may add something of importance to the issue, because I was in question, and my learned friend is right, when I raised this issue at the beginning of the trial, and indeed the memoirs of Mr. Tihic were not admitted. We objected. That's the first point. But let me refresh the memory of my friend. Maybe he didn't carefully read the transcript, or maybe he was not present in the courtroom when, after the same issue was raised, and the instruction of Judge Singh, Honourable Judge Singh who was seated there, stated that I as Defence counsel can put this issue and these topics to Mr. Tihic, not directly, but with this line of questioning. If he agrees, then it's okay. If not, then he will give some other information. In case of Mr. Izetbegovic, the issue was the following: The procedure was the following: Judge -- Honourable Judge Singh said that all these persons here are Prosecutor witnesses. So it's absolutely permissible, it's absolutely in accordance with the principle of law, to try to impeach one of the other witness of the Prosecution that way. And everything is in transcript. So it's not -- it is not absolutely founded on facts what my learned friend just said. It was the case when we were permitted by this Trial Chamber to introduce certain portions of memoirs of Sulejman Tihic. Although they are not admitted. It's just a creation of certain, I would say, supporting -- explanation of certain events of very important impact of this case. That was the case. So I just for the record want to tell you this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just respond briefly to two points. Number one, with regard to Mr. Tihic, you can impeach a witness by their prior statements if they are inconsistent. That's the rule. You can impeach with a prior inconsistent statement. Tihic came up and testified and he had a right to impeach him with any prior inconsistent statements in a book which was written by Tihic. On the other hand, if you recall when Mr. Izetbegovic got on the stand, and Mr. Pantelic tried to question him concerning a statement made by Mr. Tihic about Mr. Izetbegovic. It wasn't a complimentary statement. It was a statement where they said: Mr. Tihic said here that he wasn't happy with you because of your drinking. We objected at that time and we said you cannot impeach one witness with the statement of another. And this Court, if you want, I'll get the citation at the break, this Court refused to allow that testimony, as this Court has refused to allow any time during this trial impeaching one witness with the statement of another.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that problem, and even after Judge Singh had stated what he had stated, at a later stage it was explained that the procedure in this trial is that you don't impeach a witness with the statement of another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did not say that this was Mr. Tihic's statement. This is a piece of fiction, a literary work of Mr. Tihic. Mr. Tihic wrote it as his contribution to history or literature. This is not a statement. Mr. Tihic's statement that he gave here to the Tribunal, I did not mention to Mr. Fitozovic. I just indicated -- I just read out one piece from these memoirs. And I just wanted to ask Mr. Fitozovic whether this was true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the general meaning of "memoirs," or I think, in fact, the term "the recollections" of Mr. Tihic was used in the early stages of the trial where this was an issue, that memoirs, recollections, diaries, are not generally not viewed as works of fiction as such. So I have a little bit of a problem with you saying this is a piece of fiction, a literary work of Mr. Tihic. I can't recollect whether it was published or not. It's my feeling that it wasn't. And one of the things in issue earlier on in the trial was the fact that he had not written these memoirs contemporaneously with the events as they occurred but several years or so after the event, and so on. But that, be as it may, I don't think memoirs, recollections, diaries are necessarily going to be synonymous with works of fiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I just wanted to note on October 19th, 2001, that's where Mr. Izetbegovic was cross-examined by Pantelic concerning remarks by Mr. Tihic in his book and we objected and it was sustained because what it is is you're asking one witness to comment really on the credibility of another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that is sufficient for counsel. Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to remind the Chamber that while we were hearing the witness Kemal Mehinovic, we referred to a book of Mr. Dragan Lukac, when we told him that a murder that he mentioned did not happen in Samac but in Obudovac. So in our opinion, these are also some kinds of recollections or historical events that Mr. Lukac described, and that was not disallowed. I do not remember, however, whether the Prosecution had any objections. So in the same vein, I thought that these recollections of Mr. Tihic would have the same treatment. But if the Trial Chamber states that this should not be used, that is not a problem. We will just continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You will not use that. The incident with Dragan Lukac and I think his book is slightly different from the memoirs you are trying to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, and when you testified before this Chamber, you said that you asked for weapons from the SDA party because the Muslim population was not armed. This is page 8384, so page 8384, line 17.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this in my statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. No, not in your statement. This was not in the written statement that you gave in 1995. You said this before this Chamber, so this happened during your testimony.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase the question, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The weapons that you were seeking, you wanted to get them from the SDA party because, according to your testimony, the Muslim population was not armed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it help if he read the exact statement? He's paraphrasing, and I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe if he read from the transcript, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will ask my colleague to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... easiest way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So here it is. Page 8384: "On the executive board, I told Sulejman Tihic, the president of SDA, that the situation in the town, in municipality, and in the region was very complex, that there was a lot of weapons surrounding us, that Serbs were armed, and it was clear that none of Muslims were armed. And at that time I told Tihic, I told him the following: 'If he wanted me, I would still be the president of the safety commission, but I wanted him to get some arms so that we could also have some weapons.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This is what you said before this Trial Chamber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify a certain issue, or if you would agree with me about the following: When you used this phrase "we," did this refer to the SDA party and the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did it only refer to the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, could you tell me, then: Who did you talk about when you said "we"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The citizens of Bosanski Samac. That's who I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And you had this talk with the president of the municipal board, Sulejman Tihic, of SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Party of Democratic Action was the party of the Muslim population in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree further that members of the SDA were -- that the membership was exclusively Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that in this unit of yours, only Muslims were represented?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand this question. What do you mean, "unit of yours"?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The unit that was under your command.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't command anybody at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, then, when you started having command over this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the following: I asked from Sulejman Tihic some weapons, and I also said that Sulejman Tihic got scared by this idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, we already heard this.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mr. Sulejman Tihic, from that moment on, did not dare to do anything with things military. He didn't dare to do anything about a unit or anything like that. If you're asking questions, could you please be more specific, because I do not want to create confusion for this Honourable Chamber. I could answer one of your questions with "no," even though I might have answered a similar question by the Prosecution yesterday with "yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay, then. Here's a clearer question: When you became the commander of this military, armed unit that was in Bosanski Samac, when did you become its commander?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September there was no military armed unit in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell this Trial Chamber when this unit was created?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this happened in October or in late September.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So this means that at the end of September and in October of 1991, you created this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, Alija Fitozovic, personally created this unit, I as Alija Fitozovic, the citizen, and not the Party of Democratic Action. You said yourself earlier that members of the SDA were mostly Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let me finish. There were also Croats in this unit, and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please. We will come to that. We will come to all the members and we'll talk about who was a member there. Please do not hurry.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, please, then, let's follow a chronological order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I didn't dream up this September. You said yourself in your testimony that this happened at the end of September, that is to say, the beginning of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered the town board at the beginning of September, the board of SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This unit was created in late September/early October 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You claim, Mr. Fitozovic, that the Party of Democratic Action had nothing to do with the creation of this unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did they have anything to do with this, the SDA party? Did these two units, the SDA party and this military unit, have any contact?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you follow a chronological order, you will get the answer to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot answer you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you cannot, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The question was clear from counsel, whether the unit you were leading and the SDA party, as a political party, had any connection or any contact. So you can answer that question. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe just to speed things up, maybe the witness should be advised that in direct examination you might follow a chronological order; however, on cross-examination counsel is not required to follow a chronological order and can jump around, and that he should just be prepared for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, mean the chronological order according to the events, when questioning the witness. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He keeps saying, "You're not following chronological order." On direct, the Prosecution will do that or when they direct, they will do it, but on cross you can move all around at different times, and if they do it, you still have to answer the question. That's their prerogative how they want to ask questions on cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sure Mr. Fitozovic has understood that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, are you now ready to answer the question that I asked?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did this unit that you had the command over, did it have any contact with the SDA party and with the municipal board of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it had contact with the town board.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So with the town board. So that means, if I understood you correctly, that there had been some joint activities of the SDA town board and the command of this unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this might be a good time to take our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We'll resume our proceedings at 1805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination is continuing. Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you testified before this Trial Chamber that the unit, that military unit, was composed of Muslims, Croats, Albanians, and Roma.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the usher to show Exhibit D14/4, and the Serb version, which is D14/4 ter, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, the usher is not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I can help in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you have already seen this list in the course of the direct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You already told us that these are the people that were members of this unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read the first and last name of the person listed under 21.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Markovic Dragan, Vuka Karadzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This name --

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put this list on the ELMO. Mr. Pantelic will help you. Mr. Pantelic, you can now go back to your seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You've indicated that this person's name is Dragan Markovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, and could you agree with me, that this person comes from a mixed marriage?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please read out loud the first and last name of the person listed under 22. Zvonimir Nenadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this person is of Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at and read out the name of the person listed under 154.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzebic Ivica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that person also, this Dzebic Ivica, of Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to read out the full name of the person listed under 172.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Masic Zeljko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this person is also a Croat, of Croat ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read out the name of the person listed under 175.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milanovic Franjo, Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have another look. I think it should read Milinovic Franjo.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here Milanovic Franjo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a typing error, but at any rate is that person also a Croat?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And finally, under 194?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jurendic Ilija.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is that person also a Croat?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we agree that there are no other Croat members on this list?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So to conclude: On the list of your unit, there are only five ethnic Croats; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was in the initial stage, when the first lists were made. We can say that this is still 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you now read out the name of the person listed under 111.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I will. Limani Ljazim.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm whether this person is an ethnic Albanian.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the full name of the person listed under 150.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person listed under 150 is Bajrami Sukrija, Bulevar Revolucije Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm that the person listed under 150 is of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the full name of the person listed under 167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Pantelic, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Always in the service of justice, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 167 we have the name Idrizi Esad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that he is also an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Right here next to it, could you please read out the name of the person listed under 168.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Idrizi Rexhep.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you also agree that he's an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: And if I could just ask you to read out the full name of the person listed under 206.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Listed under 206 there is the name of Mehmedi Almir, father's name Himzije.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this person is also an ethnic Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then agree that the total number of ethnic Albanians on this list is five?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree about the fact that the five Albanians, five ethnic Albanians, that they were Muslims, that they were of the Islamic religion?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree with that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If you saw this list, and you did see this list, did you notice that on this list there isn't a single person of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice that there are no ethnic Serbs, but I have to note that this list was made in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that in this unit, in terms of percentages, there were about 98 per cent of Muslims, ethnic Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have my calculator here with me, but I trust in that your calculation is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I hope that you will agree with me that this percentage, 98 per cent of Muslims in this unit, does not reflect the ethnic composition of the town of Samac, of the town of Bosanski Samac, and of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it does not reflect the ethnic composition, the ethnic structure that existed in the municipality of Bosanski Samac and the town of Bosanski Samac, but I have to tell you that this list was made in October or September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just if I may have just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your indulgence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you still maintain that this was not a military unit of Muslims from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when this list was made, this was not a military unit at all, because a military unit has weapons. When this unit -- when this list was made, nobody had any weapons. I have already said that this list was made in September or October, right at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please specify the year for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So this list that you have before you now was made in early September -- no. In fact in late September and in early October 1991?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I make allowance for the possibility that it may have been in November.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, the existence of this unit, was it made public through the media in the town of Bosanski Samac and in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we then agree that this was a secret and illegal organisation?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can ask him if it was a public organisation. You could probably ask him if it's a secret organisation. However, to characterise it as an illegal organisation, that is a legal -- that's a legal decision or conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's a matter for submission. Yes, Counsel. Can you rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will do so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the organisation of this unit was secret, or rather, that this unit was organised secretly?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just as it is the case with the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, I really have to ask you not to make comparisons in all of your answers, but to merely answer the question.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I did not make comparisons in each of my answers, just in this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could I kindly ask you to refrain from doing that in your further answers.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Was the establishment of such units illegal and punishable in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that. Again, he's not an attorney. If they want to qualify him with some sort of legal background, I think he could answer that question, but even with qualifications it's -- if they want to bring witness on to talk about what you could legally and could not legally do, that's one thing, but to have this witness discuss off illegal conclusions is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, I hope we don't have to go through this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I counted with the fact that Mr. Fitozovic is educated enough and that he has enough knowledge, because of his education and because of his military training --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you proceed with your cross-examination? We've ruled on that. Please, just proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Fitozovic, that the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, during 1991, was still a part of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that at that time, in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as in other republics, federal and republic laws were enforced -- were in force?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they were not complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether they were in force in this territory.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was that they were not because they were not complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're going to move on to the matter of arming this military unit. You said that the first 30 automatic rifles were procured by Izet Izetbegovic for the unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. I said that I got these rifles through private channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you, Mr. Fitozovic. At first that's exactly what you said, but then, after the intervention of the Trial Chamber, you said that it was Izet Izetbegovic who did this.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. Pisarevic. I procured the weapons privately from Izet Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Izet Izetbegovic was at that time the vice-president of the Party of Democratic Action. He was the vice-president of the town board of SDA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I would like to help you here, but I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar who Mr. Izet Izetbegovic got the weapons from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I wasn't interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Senahid Mehic [As interpreted]? Did this name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means nothing to me, Senahid Mehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that among these 30 automatic rifles there were also rifles of the type of Genscher and Zagi?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we could not agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the transcript, page 60, line 25, the name is Senahid Memic, not Mehic. Instead of H, it is M. Just to make sure, because this name is going to be mentioned on other occasions, so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. That is correct, Mr. Pisarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you did not receive any rifle of the type of Zagi in this delivery?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In your unit, did you have this type of rifle? Did have you this automatic rifle, Zagi?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You are a military person. You have some military knowledge. Could you explain to me what kind of weapon this rifle is, this Zagi automatic rifle?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zagi is a rifle manufactured in Croatia. They were the ones who were making these rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This type of arms appeared for the first time in the theatres in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you, from Mr. Izet Izetbegovic, receive five pistols with the calibre 7.62 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you receive from Mr. Izet Izetbegovic sets of 120 bullets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did a certain person of Muslim ethnicity who had a white Golf car with Sarajevo licence plates SA335820, in December, bring some ammunition to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree -- in other words, are you aware that at that time, the procurement of automatic rifles was illegal?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there had been any automatic military weapons in the open markets?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right, then. Could you buy these things in shops where other weapons were sold?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So it is your claim that in 1991, automatic military arms could be bought in weapons stores, quite openly, in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not talking about Yugoslavia; I'm talking about the town of Bosanski Samac. It is my claim that in Bosanski Samac, these arms could be bought, and not only in shops that were specialised or registered for selling weapons of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could we then agree that that kind of purchase was illegal?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything was legal at that time. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. You can ask if he's aware of certain laws, but you could have a law, but something can still be legal because it could be -- it could occur under duress, it could occur in different circumstances that -- he can ask him, he can read a law to him and say were you aware of this law or were you aware that there were laws on this, relating to this issue, relating to the procurement of weapons, the possession of weapons. But to ask if a particular purchase is legal or illegal, then you need a -- I'd at least argue you need someone to offer a legal conclusion, and this is not the witness to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think let's do it this way, Mr. Pisarevic. This is a fact witness, and you deal with facts, all right? Let him answer his questions, right? Now if any of the answers amount to what is illegal, in your view, then you deal with that by way of submission at the end of the case, so that we avoid this problem of coming into the legality of whatever was being done, with a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel does not have the mike on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In what shops in Bosanski Samac could automatic military weapons be bought, then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such shops in the town. I said earlier, they weren't only meant for selling arms. You could buy it, for example, at the Spriceraj [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What is that? Where was this Spriceraj?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, my next question is going to be: What shop was this, and who was the owner of that shop in which you could buy automatic military rifles?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, automatic weapons could be bought in the shop that belonged to Mrs. Simo Zaric. She had a general type store.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, Mr. Fitozovic, who bought these military weapons in the shop that belonged to Mrs. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could tell you who the weapons were bought from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, my question was: Who bought the weapons? You had already said earlier who the weapons were bought from. Could you please tell me: Who bought the automatic military rifles in the store belonging to Mrs. Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bahrija Vajzovic bought it. He paid 1,000 -- 100 Deutschmarks for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, Bahrija Vajzovic is dead; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you mentioned another procurement of automatic rifles. In November of 1991, when a truck belonging to a Slovenian company, Viator, broke down, this truck was transferring weapons to Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this transfer of weapons was done with other members of your unit in the warehouse of the Sarajevo brewery?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This warehouse of the Sarajevo brewery is at the mouth of Bosna into Sava, above the embankment that is around the Gacko Naselje [pheon]?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This transfer was done there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area is open to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Fitozovic, Namik Suljic, who at that time, in November 1991, was the assistant to the police commander in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Namik Suljic is a Muslim; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure that he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm the fact that it was in fact Namik Suljic, as the assistant to the police commander in Bosanski Samac, during the transfer of the weapons in this public place, secured and made sure that the transfer was successful?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You transferred the weapons to a truck that was owned by the veterinary station in Bosanski Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: That truck was not owned by Smail Smailovic, a member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Smail Smailovic was just the driver of the truck in the veterinary station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was an employee of the veterinary station and his profession was driver. So you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can a driver take a vehicle which is not his property --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object again, Your Honour. We're getting back into legal decisions, whether a person is allowed to take them off time, what access anyone has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I wanted the question completed. Maybe counsel can complete the question and let's see whether it's objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How do you explain the fact that the driver, Smail Smailovic, was able to take the truck of the veterinary station and use it for party purposes?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what party purposes are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific. The transfer of weapons.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The party that you're implicating had nothing to do with the transfer of weapons. It was a political party. It was not registered for that kind of activity. It was not a service company that would engage in transfers of this kind, or any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Right at the beginning I told you that it was -- I put it to you that it was your unit that did it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that unit had nothing to do with the Party of Democratic Action. How long do we have to go on like this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, we have already heard this statement of yours, but you failed to respond to my question. How do you explain that the driver, Smail Smailovic, was able to take the truck from the veterinary station, of his own free will, and use it for the transfer of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's quite apparent that he took it of his own will, and he probably should be held responsible by somebody. I assume that somebody would have to be his immediate superior in the veterinary station. Now, whether he was actually held responsible for this, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The weapons were transferred -- I mean, you organised the transfer of the weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Could we please remove this list from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the usher to remove the list from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, did you perhaps hear, whether Mr. Sulejman Tihic was in any way involved in this operation of the transfer of weapons near or at the Sarajevo brewery warehouse?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was not involved in this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: After the operation was completed, did you in any way notify Mr. Sulejman Tihic about the event?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So in other words, Mr. Tihic does not know about the transfer of weapons from the truck that had broken down in Samac --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Counsel is asking this witness about the knowledge of Sulejman Tihic. Sulejman Tihic could have heard about this incident from anyone involved or from anyone who was told by anyone involved about the incident therefore he would have knowledge. The fact that this person didn't tell Sulejman Tihic doesn't mean he has knowledge about it. He can't answer for Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Tihic never learned from you about the transfer of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't tell him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Izet Izetbegovic the vice-president of the SDA, the town board, involved in any way in this operation?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we agreed before that Mr. Izet Izetbegovic held this post or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's immaterial now.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not notified. I mean, I did not notify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please list all the persons that took part in the transfer.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember all the names. Could I perhaps do it some other time, later on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any names at all?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember myself. In the meantime, there was a war, and I forgot a lot of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, you were also a member of the executive board of the town board of the SDA for Bosanski Samac, and you were the president of the safety and security commission?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You took part in the work of the party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, and do you indeed have any information about the fact that the SDA in the town of Samac carried out certain activities aimed at gathering some funds for the operation of the party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So you claim that the SDA in Samac did not have an action in which it collected voluntary contributions from Muslim citizens in Samac?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did conduct such an action, such a campaign.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what were the results of the campaign?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Positive. They were positive. They were satisfactory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Since you were such a high-ranking official in the party --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll let him finish the question, but "since you were such a high-a ranking official in the party," there's been no evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. Let counsel complete the question and then the witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you, and in what way, take part in the making of the decisions on how the funds would be used, the funds that were at the disposal of the party?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, we have to define quite clearly what funds we're talking about. The funds that were gathered or some other funds? Because we're wasting time here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: My question was about the funds of the town board of the SDA in Bosanski Samac. I asked you about the voluntary contributions campaign for another reason. Now I'm asking you: Did you, as, in my opinion, a high-ranking official in the party, because you were a member of the executive board and you were the president of the Safety and Security Commission, so did you take part in the decision-making process about the way in which the funds that the party had would be spent? I hope that now you understand my question.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that I understand is that there were no rules in the Party of Democratic Action that would determine who defined who a high-ranking official in the party would be. So I don't know whether I was a high-ranking official, a lower-ranking official. There were no ranks. There were no rules indicating who a high-ranking official in the party would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Fitozovic, did you take part at all in the decision-making process about the way in which the funds at the disposal of the SDA party were used?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA FITOZOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I believe our time is up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. How much more time do you need for cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. You've taken one and a half hours already. Unless you are cross-examining on behalf of everybody. You've taken one and a half hours already.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in light of everything that this witness has said and everything that he hasn't said, this is the time that I require.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We have to cut down on that. You have to cut down on that. And one way of cutting down is you should not repeat the examination-in-chief, for instance, because I observed that that is always done, and that takes double the time. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would merely like to point to the fact that in the pre-trial brief, the Prosecution indicated that it would be questioning this witness for three to four hours, and the Prosecution also indicated that the questioning today would last about 45 minutes, yet it lasted about an hour and a half. And the Prosecution questioned this witness for three days, and this witness is of such importance that we cannot really limit our examination in any way. Mr. Pisarevic, of course, asked some of the questions that I intend to ask, but I can inform the Trial Chamber that I plan to conduct my cross-examination for an hour to two hours. But I cannot be as clear in my statement because I don't know what questions that I intended to ask Mr. Pisarevic may have -- may ask tomorrow. But I believe that my cross-examination would end within an hour and a half. I will not be repeating all the questions that Mr. Pisarevic will ask, but I will probably cover some of the same topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, of course I will try to reduce the time according to the questions and the area which will be probably covered by my colleagues, friends. So I will do really my best to reduce the time. I already produced and gave to my learned friend from the Prosecution certain documents. So depending on the way how this witness will respond, it will be very short questions, very simple. We have five or six copies, I mean not more than ten minutes it will be for these papers. And about the other questions and areas, roughly saying one hour. But even less. Even less, according to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Depending on the other questions from the other colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to respond to Mr. Lukic when he was talking about the length of time the Prosecution takes. Of course the Prosecution takes longer because the Prosecution has to adduce evidence to cover liability of each and every accused. Yes. That is understood. Whereas each accused has got his own defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just two very brief points. One is: When this witness is taken out could the Registry ask the people who transport the witness back and forth to the hotel to bring him in about 25 minutes earlier so I can go through all these documents that were given to me this afternoon? Instead -- I think they usually bring him here about let's say 2.00, if they could bring him here maybe 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Who does that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The transporting group from the Victims and Witnesses. When the usher brings this witness out, if he could ask the transporting people to bring him here 20 minutes to 2.00 tomorrow so I can go through these documents and he will still have about 10 minutes to relax before he goes back on the stand for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber would request that that be done to assist the Prosecution to deal with the documents that have just been handed to the Prosecution I think today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Regarding this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the -- I was just going to say, the other thing is: I know I've gone over the time. I thought I'd only have him on for a day and a half. But I concede this is a significant witness and being a significant witness not only for the Prosecution, it does affect the Defence. So I wouldn't object if he wants to take the extra time, but I just ask that they don't ask the same questions over and over and just repeat direct. I would not object to them taking what time that's necessary because it is a significant witness and I'd worry about an appellate issue if we ever get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of course the Trial Chamber is aware that they have the right to cross-examine. It's just that they should avoid repeating the same questions and repeating examination-in-chief answers. All right. We shall adjourn -- I think the Registry has something to say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. If I may just re-explain to the Prosecution that the message cannot be passed to the transport people of the Victims and Witnesses. They have been informed that they have to make the request tomorrow morning to Simo the chief of the section of Victims and Witnesses, and that's how it has to be arranged. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will do that in the morning, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will rise and continue tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of May 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
